mainEntity.name: How much does a Volkswagen Sharan 1.4 TSI or 2.0 TSI engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a Volkswagen Sharan 1.4 TSI (EA111), expect £2,500-£4,000 supply-only for a rebuilt unit, or £600-£1,200 for a used engine. For the 2.0 TSI (DEDA), rebuilt units typically range £3,800-£5,500, with used options from £1,200-£2,200. Fitting adds approximately £520-£650 labour at UK specialist rates.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a Volkswagen Sharan 1.4 TSI or 2.0 TSI?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common warning sign on EA111 1.4 TSI and EA888 2.0 TSI engines is a rattling noise on cold start lasting 1-3 seconds. This is the tensioner losing hydraulic pressure. Other symptoms include engine management light illumination, timing-related fault codes, and eventually misfiring or non-start if the chain jumps.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Volkswagen Sharan 1.4 TSI or 2.0 TSI?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on your Sharan's value. On examples worth under £5,000: a used engine at £600-£1,200 plus fitting often makes more sense than a rebuilt unit. On cars worth £6,000+: a rebuilt engine at £2,500-£5,500 is financially viable and carries a 12-month warranty, which a used engine typically doesn't.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the Volkswagen Sharan 1.4 TSI CAVA and CTHA engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both are 1.4-litre EA111 engines producing 148hp (150 PS). The CAVA (2010-2015) was the original 1.4 TSI engine in the second-generation Sharan. The CTHA (2012-2015) was introduced later with minor calibration differences. Both share the same timing chain tensioner weakness and carbon buildup issues.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Volkswagen Sharan 1.4 TSI or 2.0 TSI engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A straight engine swap on a Volkswagen Sharan 1.4 TSI or 2.0 TSI typically takes 8-10 hours labour at a specialist, including transfer of ancillary components. Most workshops complete the job in 1-2 working days.

mainEntity.name: Is the Volkswagen Sharan 1.4 TSI or 2.0 TSI engine reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The EA111 1.4 TSI (CAVA, CAVB, CTHA, CTHB, 2010-2015) has a known timing chain tensioner weakness that makes it unreliable if not proactively maintained - tensioner failure can occur from 60,000 miles. The EA888 2.0 TSI (DEDA, 2015-2020) is more robust but still has timing chain concerns on early units. Both engines suffer from carbon buildup on intake valves due to direct injection. Rebuilt units include upgraded components addressing original flaws.

historyTimeline.h2: Volkswagen Sharan 1.4 TSI & 2.0 TSI - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Volkswagen Sharan 1.4 TSI and 2.0 TSI arrived with the second-generation Sharan (Typ 7N) in 2010 as the premium petrol options, offering families a refined alternative to diesel power. The 1.4 TSI spanned both the EA111 and EA211 engine families across the 7N generation, while the 2.0 TSI (DEDA) arrived in 2015 as the range-topping petrol option with 220hp.

milestones.description: Second-generation Sharan (Typ 7N) launches with 1.4 TSI CAVA engine, 148hp (150 PS), EA111 twincharger (turbo + supercharger)
CAVB introduced alongside CAVA, sharing the same 148hp output with minor calibration differences
CTHA/CTHB engines introduced for the 1.4 TSI, retaining the EA111 twincharger design
1.4 TSI switches to EA211 turbocharged engine (no supercharger) with improved reliability
2.0 TSI DEDA introduced, 220hp EA888 engine, 350Nm torque
End of Sharan production; 1.4 TSI and 2.0 TSI remain popular used engine replacements

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Volkswagen Sharan 1.4 TSI and 2.0 TSI is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Volkswagen Sharan 1.4 TSI & 2.0 TSI Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Volkswagen Sharan 1.4 TSI and 2.0 TSI present distinct reliability profiles depending on which engine family you have. Early EA111 1.4 TSI units (CAVA, CAVB, CTHA, CTHB, 2010-2015) are known for timing chain tensioner failure and carbon buildup. The EA888 2.0 TSI (DEDA, 2015-2020) shares similar timing chain concerns but is generally more robust. Rebuilt Volkswagen Sharan 1.4 TSI and 2.0 TSI engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded timing components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Tensioner Failure - Why the Volkswagen Sharan 1.4 TSI EA111 Wears Prematurely
problems.affectedModels: Volkswagen Sharan 1.4 TSI (CAVA, CAVB, CTHA, CTHB - 2010-2015, EA111 engines)
problems.rootCause: The EA111 1.4 TSI uses a timing chain on the gearbox side of the engine with a plastic tensioner that loses hydraulic pressure. Chain stretch and tensioner wear cause rattling on cold start; if ignored, the chain can jump timing or snap, destroying the engine.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Full chain kit, tensioner, guides, camshaft sprockets
repairOptions.longevity: Best before failure - catches it early if you hear cold-start rattle

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded timing components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If chain has already failed or mileage over 120k - replacement often cheaper than dealer repair

problems.recommendation: If your Volkswagen Sharan 1.4 TSI is rattling on cold start, book a timing chain inspection immediately. Preventative chain replacement at £800-£1,500 from a specialist is far cheaper than a rebuilt engine. If the chain has already jumped or broken, compare a used engine (under £1,800 fitted if value-conscious) against a rebuilt unit (£2,500-£4,000) - the rebuilt premium buys warranty protection against the same tensioner failure recurring.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt CAVA/CTHA Volkswagen Sharan 1.4 TSI engine prices

problems.h4: Timing Chain Tensioner Failure - Why the Volkswagen Sharan 2.0 TSI EA888 Wears Prematurely
problems.rootCause: Early EA888 2.0 TSI engines use a timing chain tensioner with a plastic collar that can fail, allowing the chain to slacken. If the chain jumps timing, it can cause catastrophic engine damage as it is an interference motor.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Full chain kit, upgraded tensioner, guides
repairOptions.longevity: Best before failure - catches it early if you hear cold-start rattle

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded timing components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If chain has already failed or engine has jumped timing

problems.vehicleValueCheck: The Volkswagen Sharan 2.0 TSI typically sits in the £6,000-£14,000 value bracket. A rebuilt engine at £3,800-£5,500 represents 25-50% of vehicle value on most examples, making replacement financially viable. For sub-£6,000 examples, a used engine at £1,200-£2,200 plus fitting may be the more sensible option.
problems.recommendation: If your Volkswagen Sharan 2.0 TSI is rattling on cold start, book a timing chain inspection immediately. The upgraded tensioner design in later EA888 engines is more reliable, but early DEDA units (2015-2017) are most at risk. Preventative chain replacement at £1,000-£1,800 is far cheaper than a rebuilt engine.

problems.h4: Carbon Buildup on Intake Valves - Why the Volkswagen Sharan 1.4/2.0 TSI Loses Power
problems.affectedModels: Volkswagen Sharan 1.4 TSI (EA111) and 2.0 TSI (EA888) - all direct-injection TSI engines
problems.rootCause: Direct injection petrol engines do not have fuel washing over the intake valves, allowing oil and carbon deposits to accumulate. This restricts airflow, causing misfires, reduced power, and rough idle.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Intake manifold removal, media blasting of valves
Supply & fit, includes cleaned/replaced intake components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Only if carbon buildup has caused valve damage or if engine has other issues

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A £400-£700 walnut blasting service is routine maintenance on any direct-injection TSI engine. Even on sub-£4,000 examples, the repair is well within the vehicle's value. Full replacement is not justified for carbon buildup alone - only escalate if valve damage has occurred.
problems.recommendation: If your Volkswagen Sharan 1.4 TSI or 2.0 TSI feels down on power, has rough idle, or misfires under load, book a walnut blasting service with a specialist (£400-£700). This is particularly important on EA111 and EA888 engines approaching 60,000-80,000 miles.
